title: Integral Chow modification with a relatively ample projective-space line bundle
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme], separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exist an integer $N\geq0$, an integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme $Y$, a proper surjective $k$-morphism $\pi:Y\to X$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism], an immersion $j:Y\to\mathbf P^N_k$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], and a nonempty open $U\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism. The invertible module $\mathcal L=j^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_k}(1)$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-projective-space-twist, def-sc-invertible-module] is $\pi$-relatively ample: for every affine open $W\subseteq X$, $\mathcal L|_{\pi^{-1}(W)}$ is ample [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. No properness hypothesis on $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is made.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian: its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. Thus $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian, and $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] to $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, obtaining $N$, $\pi_0:Z\to X$ proper surjective, an immersion $j_0:Z\to\mathbf P^N_k$ over $k$, and a dense open $U_0\subset X$ over which $\pi_0$ is an isomorphism. Since $X$ is integral it is nonempty, so $U_0$ is nonempty; choose a nonempty affine open $U\subset U_0$. It remains dense because $X$ is irreducible. Properness implies finite type, and composition preserves finite type (compose the affine-local finite algebra generating sets and quasi-compact maps). Hence $Z$ is finite type over $k$ and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

Identify $V=\pi_0^{-1}(U)$ with $U$ and let $h:V\hookrightarrow Z$ be its open immersion. The scheme $Z$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]; since $V$ is affine, $h$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. Let $c:Y\hookrightarrow Z$ be its scheme-theoretic image. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-ideal-qc], $V$ factors through $Y$ and $|Y|$ is the closure of $V$ in $Z$. By [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-restrict-open], restriction to $V$ gives the scheme-theoretic image of $\mathrm{id}_V$, which is $V$ (its defining kernel is zero). Thus $c^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism, and $V$ is a dense nonempty open subscheme of $Y$.

The closure of the irreducible space $V\simeq U$ is irreducible: if covered by two closed subsets, intersect with $V$; one contains all of $V$, hence its closure. To check reducedness, on every affine open $B\subset Z$ the ideal of $Y\cap B$ is $I_B=\ker(\mathcal O_Z(B)\to\mathcal O_V(B\cap V))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel]. Every local ring of the integral $V$ is a domain by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field]; consequently a nilpotent section of $\mathcal O_V$ is zero, since every germ is zero. Thus $a^r\in I_B$ implies $a\in I_B$, so each $\mathcal O_Z(B)/I_B$ is reduced. These affines cover $Y$, proving it reduced. The equivalence in [def-pc-integral-scheme] now proves $Y$ integral. This writes out the reducedness assertion of Remark 0201 (3), rather than assuming arbitrary Chow modifications integral.

Put $\pi=\pi_0\circ c$ and $j=j_0\circ c$. A closed immersion is proper and proper morphisms compose by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], so $\pi$ is proper. Its image is closed by the definition of properness, and contains the dense open $U$ because $\pi^{-1}(U)=c^{-1}(V)\simeq V\simeq U$; therefore it is all of $X$. The map $j$ is an immersion by the composition clause of the same permanence lemma. Since $\pi$ and $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are separated, their composite is separated. They are of finite type, so their composite is of finite type as in step 1. This supplies all the asserted geometric properties of $Y,\pi,j,U$.

Form $a=(j,\pi):Y\to\mathbf P^N_k\times_k X=\mathbf P^N_X$. It is an immersion by [lem-chow-tuple-immersion], applied to the two $k$-morphisms $j$ and $\pi$. The projection $q:\mathbf P^N_X\to X$ is proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence separated. As $q\circ a=\pi$ is proper, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] proves that $a$ is proper. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] proves that $a$ is a closed immersion. Only $\pi$, not $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, was required to be proper.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts] with the finite nonempty coordinate set $\{0,\ldots,N\}$. Its clauses (a),(b) provide the covering by the pulled-back opens $D_+(T_i)$ and free generators $T_i$ of the pullback of the Proj twist from $\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf Z}$, with $T_i=(T_i/T_j)T_j$ on overlaps. Over $\operatorname{Spec}k$, clause (c) identifies these charts with $\operatorname{Spec}k[T_l/T_i:l\ne i]$. On their overlaps, sending the generator $e_i^{(1)}$ in [def-pc-projective-space-twist] to $T_i$ respects exactly the relation $e_i^{(1)}=(T_i/T_j)e_j^{(1)}$; the resulting local isomorphisms therefore glue. This identifies the line bundle used in the statement with the pullback of the Proj twist from $\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf Z}$. For $r:\mathbf P^N_X\to\mathbf P^N_k$ the second projection, the projections $\rho_X:\mathbf P^N_X\to\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf Z}$ and $\rho_k:\mathbf P^N_k\to\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf Z}$ satisfy $\rho_k\circ r=\rho_X$, by the fibre-product universal property. Thus pullback composition [def-pc-module-pullback] gives $r^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_k}(1)\cong\rho_X^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf Z}}(1)=\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_X}(1)$ and, since $r\circ a=j$, $\mathcal L\cong a^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_X}(1)$. The chart generators also prove invertibility. For every affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset X$, the base change $a_W:\pi^{-1}(W)\to\mathbf P^N_A$ of the closed immersion $a$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (b). Its composite with the structural projection is the restriction of $\pi$. The same equality of projections to $\mathbf P^N_{\mathbf Z}$ and pullback composition identify $a_W^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^N_A}(1)$ with $\mathcal L|_{\pi^{-1}(W)}$, using exactly the definition of the twist in [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible]. That theorem now proves this restriction invertible and ample. Since $W$ is arbitrary this is the required relative ampleness. For the empty affine open the inverse image is empty, quasi-compactness holds, and the affine nonvanishing-cover condition is vacuous.
